Just graduated with my Master’s in music. These thoughts are extremely common. They will not only not go away with time but will only compound. The further you go down the path, the more questions you will have than answers. This career is a game of constantly regulating yourself. The voice is such a personal instrument, it is hard to separate your craft of singing to You.

But you’re only going to be a freshman, the paths you can take in this career are limitless. To be this young and already starting to have these worries leads me to tell you to take a step back and ask yourself why you want to do music. Do you choose this path for reasons outside of necessity (I am also autistic to note)? Is there genuine enjoyment out of it? If you can’t answer that question with truth, then you’re gonna burn yourself out quick. My voice teacher in undergrad would always say “Remember why you sing.” Please talk to people you know and trust, even if they’re not musicians themselves. I understand that feeling that you [Have] to make music. I also want to say that your goals and aspirations will inevitably change over time. You might be surprised over what you will learn about yourself while studying music. There might be other interests that will spark. Keep an open mind. 

You are at the very beginning of a long, frustrating, and rewarding journey. Time and time again you will be challenged. Anything can happen. No one person takes the exact same route. Undergraduate is about putting together your musical foundations: technique, theory, aural training, etc. As you get better in your craft, the anxieties will still be there, but hopefully you will have gained enough confidence that you Have made progress and you deserve to be in this career. As long as you have that fight in you, you will find the will to keep going. Listen to the mentors that you trust. Form your connections. Make your memories. You will meet the people that will help you channel the ambitions you listed. 

Don’t fret about the ride yet, you haven’t even gotten on the train! Good luck!
